assessments.reasoning: The Release 754 Views topic first specifies DEFINE VIEW in CDS DDL and identifies activation as creating two ABAP Dictionary objects. The separate descriptions identify the CDS entity and the CDS database view, distinguishing the latter from the corresponding SQL view.

The pinned original Linguist implementation registers a category named ABAP CDS with .asddls and source.abapcds. It supplies classifier context. The category label does not independently assert that the technology or DCL is equivalent to DDL.

The pinned Linguist association sample starts with @AbapCatalog.sqlViewName and uses DEFINE VIEW with a select and association. It illustrates the specific DDL form and naming convention without providing activation results or a SAP release pin.

The pinned Linguist parameters sample starts with @AbapCatalog.sqlViewName and uses DEFINE VIEW with parameters and a SELECT source. Its syntax illustrates the DDIC-based declaration form, and it supplies no evidence of activation or host compatibility.

challenge.method: Compare the Release 754 activation paragraphs with the pinned DDL examples and SAP’s separate documentation for DEFINE VIEW ENTITY. Check whether the underlying database SQL view or a newer CDS view form would alter the ABAP Dictionary object count.
challenge.results: The release page names two ABAP Dictionary objects for the scoped DDIC-based form. It separately mentions the underlying database SQL view. The newer CDS view-entity statement has its own reference and does not broaden this claim.

limitations: The claim covers the documented DDIC-based view form. DEFINE VIEW ENTITY, abstract CDS entities, access-control definitions and downstream database behavior have distinct evidentiary scopes.
